subject: Urgent: Corral plan for Valora checkout congestion and SLA exposure
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@valora.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Valora SRE <sre@valora.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@valora.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Checkout failures this morning — urgent

Vivek / Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike in 5xxs and very long completion times on our checkout flows between 08:20–09:05 PST. Token consumption is normal but the long-tail (p95->p999) has blown out — many customers hit a stalled checkout and drop. Attached are a few trace samples and a screenshot showing a cluster of 502/504 responses.

Impact: higher error rates and throughput collapse for a subset of requests using your hosted endpoint (model: rwd-3b-compact). We need immediate mitigation and an ETA on root cause — this is affecting our busiest window and will likely trigger our renewal review next month.

Can you please:
- Confirm whether this is a regional capacity or queueing issue on Redwood's side
- Share any mitigation steps you can take in the next 60 minutes (circuit-breaker, isolate model variant, capacity bump)
- Confirm if we should expect any SLA credits if this is platform-side?

I appreciate the quick response — I'll be on the phone with the ops team.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform, Valora Commerce
elena@valora.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: valora-tail-examples.pdf, screenshot-500s.png

Elena — thanks for flagging and for the artifacts. We're investigating now. Quick notes:
- I've paged on-call infra and Eng (Dev) and looped in CS (Hannah) and our ops lead (Marissa).
- Immediate mitigation we can try: roll traffic to rwd-3b-stable (compatible variant) and temporarily raise concurrency cap for the Valora tenant in us-west region to reduce queueing. We can do that within ~10–15 minutes if Valora approves a short failover.
- I'll hold an exec-level sync at +30 to confirm next steps and resource action.

Can you join a quick bridge? I'm proposing 09:35 PST. If you have a short list of impacted routes (checkout/confirm), send them now.

Vivek

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures this morning — urgent

Summary of rapid triage (09:36):
- Root signal: per-host request queue depth spiked in us-west shard A; backlog led to persistent worker-axis contention and inflight queueing.
- Observed behavior: concurrency cap on the rwd-3b-compact variant for shared-hosting customers was reached for Valora's tenant ID (tenant isolation burst pattern). When caps hit, requests are queued instead of fast-failing; queueing led to KV cache thrashing and end-to-end latency escalations (p95 -> p999).
- Error profile: transient 502/504 from upstream worker timeouts plus a small fraction of model OOMs that triggered retries.

Immediate actions taken (09:34–09:40):
1) Raised per-tenant concurrency cap from 16 -> 40 for Valora on shard us-west-A as a stopgap (this drained queues within ~8 minutes).
2) Enabled request shedding policy for high-depth queues in the affected shard to fast-fail non-checkout routes and preserve checkout throughput.
3) Rolled a subset (20%) of Valora traffic to rwd-3b-stable (less aggressive memory profile) to reduce KV churn.

Next steps (investigation):
- Collect detailed worker traces for the 08:20–09:05 window (attached).
- Validate that our autoscaling decisions didn't create oscillation with Valora's traffic pattern.
- Propose long-term: tenant-aware queueing policy adjustments and an SLA exception discussion for dedicated pool if traffic pattern recurs.

I'll keep the thread updated with logs and a proposed action matrix.

Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: corral-action-matrix.xlsx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@valora.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures this morning — urgent

Elena — thank you and sorry for the disruption. Quick customer-facing notes and asks:
- What we heard: a congestive event in us-west affecting a subset of Valora tenant traffic; Redwood took mitigation steps (cap bump, shedding, partial variant roll).
- Immediate offer: we'll issue a one-off credit against Valora's Nov invoice (amount TBD) while we complete RCA. We will confirm amount after we quantify duration and customer impact.
- For now, can Valora confirm whether the partial failover to rwd-3b-stable is acceptable to keep live while we complete the deeper fix? That will minimize risk of re-trigger during peak.

I'll schedule a postmortem readout with you and your SREs for Tue 11/30 at 11:00 PST; if that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures this morning — urgent

Follow-up and exec summary from the readout (Tue 12/01 16:00 PST):
- Root cause: tenant burst pattern + conservative per-tenant concurrency cap on shared variant led to queue pileup and KV hot-shard churn. The policy to queue rather than fast-fail created long-tail latency.
- Impact window: 08:20–09:05 PST on 2026-11-29; estimated affected requests: ~42k; visible p99+ regressions at +2500ms on checkout endpoints.
- Short-term mitigations completed: per-tenant cap bump, selective variant roll (~20% traffic), and shedding of non-critical routes. Those reduced p99 by ~65% within 8 minutes.
- Remediation plan (owners & ETA):
  * Dev: PR for tenant-aware caps + predictive shedding rules (hotfix in 48–72h)
  * Marcus Lin: telemetry dashboard for tenant queue depth + alerting (24h)
  * Hannah: customer credit proposal and postmortem deck (24h)
  * Marissa: SL escalation for larger accounts and decision on dedicated pool offers (72h)

SLA credit stance: we will provisionally commit to a credit discussion. Final credit amount will be calculated after we finish impact quantification; Hannah will share a draft credit matrix by EOD Wednesday.

Action items (quick):
- Dev: open RED-9123 (triage + config PR link) and link corral-action-matrix.xlsx.
- Marcus: enable tenant depth alerts on us-west-A.
- Hannah: send proposed credit ranges to Valora and cc finance@redwood.com.

Elena — thank you for the logs you shared; they were instrumental. We'll keep the cadence tight until the policy change is in place. Please reach out directly if anything degrades.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
CTO, Redwood Inference
